evidence.quote: In my view, this proposition seems highly unlikely. At a minimum, it is premature.
Greenlaw and his coauthors also note that we have the flexibility to normalize the balance sheet more slowly.
I do not personally see fiscal dominance as high on the list of near term risks.
There are legitimate concerns associated with the costs and benefits of continuing asset purchases.
In particular, the authors join others in finding that accommodative monetary policy is often associated with successful fiscal consolidations.

parsed.rationale: The speech mainly rebuts the claim that fiscal pressures threaten near-term monetary policy, defends LSAPs and Fed independence, and notes the balance sheet could be normalized more slowly, a mildly dovish tilt. It gives little direct guidance on rates, and its acknowledgment of the costs of continued purchases keeps the net signal near neutral.
